- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.5) or neutral (0.0–0.25), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–4 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with recent 5–7 day trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in bullish sentiment periods; apply 2–4% downward bias if sentiment > 0.6 over last 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
